description:
Part of epic ag-o6z; read it first.

## Goal

Every webhook delivery that passes the signature check is (a) archived raw in the telemetry store, and (b) indexed by one small row in Postgres, whatever its event. Today only `workflow_run` deliveries that touch a known run leave a row, and the raw body goes only to the Railway log.

## Where the code is

- internal/webapi/api.go, func webhook: signature check, the `webhook body` log line (added in commit 5d56a21), delivery-ID check, the `workflow_run` filter.
- internal/forward/forward.go: Forwarder (background queue, POST to `OTLP_FORWARD_URL` + `/v1/<signal>`, Basic auth). Nil forwarder = forwarding off. cmd/agbredo/main.go wires it (`forward.New(os.Getenv("OTLP_FORWARD_URL"), ...)`).
- internal/core/worker.go, func ApplyLifecycle: today the only writer of `webhook_deliveries`, inside the run's transaction, as the dedupe of redeliveries.
- migrations/001_initial.sql: `webhook_deliveries(id text PRIMARY KEY, received_at timestamptz)`.

## What to build

1. Archive. In `webhook`, after the signature and delivery-ID checks, hand the raw body to the forwarder as one OTLP log record (a new method, e.g. `Forwarder.SendWebhook(delivery, event string, body []byte, attrs map[string]string)`). Shape, built by Agbredo (not `Label`, which edits a sender's payload):
   - resourceLogs[0].resource.attributes: `service.name` = `agbredo-github-webhooks`.
   - one logRecord: `timeUnixNano`/`observedTimeUnixNano` = receive time, `severityText` INFO, `body.stringValue` = the raw JSON body unchanged, attributes `github.delivery`, `github.event`, `github.action`, `github.repository` (full_name, if any), `github.installation_id` (if any), `github.sender` (sender.login, if any).
   - POST to `/v1/logs` like telemetry logs. Send the OpenObserve header `stream-name: github_webhooks` so webhooks get their own stream, if OpenObserve's OTLP endpoint honours it (check its docs; if not, drop the header and rely on `service.name`). Keep the existing failure policy: best effort, never fail the webhook, log drops.
   - Read `action`, `repository.full_name`, `installation.id`, `sender.login` with a small tolerant struct; a payload without them is still archived.
2. Index. Migration 007: add nullable columns to `webhook_deliveries`: `event text`, `action text`, `repository text`, `installation_id bigint`, `outcome text` (`handled`, `ignored`, `failed`), `error text`. Old rows keep NULLs. Every verified delivery gets a row.
   Keep the redelivery behaviour: a delivery that failed must be processed again when GitHub redelivers it; one that was handled must not be applied twice. Today that comes from inserting the row inside ApplyLifecycle's transaction. One way: the handled path writes `outcome='handled'` inside its transaction as today; ignored events insert `ignored`; on failure, upsert `failed` + error in a separate statement, and let the handled path overwrite a `failed` row (`ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE webhook_deliveries.outcome IS DISTINCT FROM 'handled'`). Note that run events already have stable IDs, so a replay of a status change is harmless.
3. Remove the `webhook body` log line from api.go. Keep the short `webhook received` / `webhook rejected` lines.
4. Deliveries refused before the signature check (bad signature, too large) are not archived (we cannot trust them); they stay in the log only, as now.

## Docs

docs/10-design.md: Parts (telemetry store also keeps webhook deliveries), Data (`webhook_deliveries` now indexes every verified delivery), Trust (raw payloads with emails and commit messages go to the store, never to Postgres or logs). docs/20-routes.md, webhook section. README.md, the OTLP_FORWARD_URL paragraph.

## How to check

- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`, with AGBREDO_TEST_DATABASE_URL set (throwaway postgres:17-alpine) for the store paths.
- Unit test the log record shape in internal/forward/forward_test.go.
- api_test: an ignored event (e.g. `ping`, `pull_request`) is archived and indexed `ignored`; a bad signature is neither; a workflow_run for an unknown run is `ignored`; a failed apply is `failed` and a redelivery then succeeds.
- After deploy: trigger a workflow in a repo with the App, find the delivery in OpenObserve (stream github_webhooks or default) and its row in Postgres.

## Open questions for Matt

- Retention of the github_webhooks stream in OpenObserve (design doc already says retention is undecided).
title: Archive every verified webhook delivery to OpenObserve and index it in Postgres
